5700.name: Entrance to the Academy

north.description: To the north lies The Eastern Gatehouse.

south.description: To the south lies The Northern Side of the Academy.

5700.description:
A forecourt of raked white gravel lies before the Academy, edged with
clipped box hedges and two stone urns of rosemary. The Eastern Gatehouse
stands a short way to the north, its lanterns pale in the daylight, and
the murmur of the Trade Road drifts from it. To the south a flight of
shallow marble steps rises to bronze-banded doors left open to the
morning. Carved across the lintel in letters a hand deep is a single
word.

extra_descs.lintel word letters carved:
The word is Inquire, cut deep and gilded once, the gilt now mostly worn
to a few bright flecks.

5701.name: The Northern Side of the Academy

north.description: To the north lies Entrance to the Academy.

east.description: To the east lies The North Wing.

south.description: To the south lies In the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The North Wing.

5701.description:
You stand in the vestibule of the Academy, a long hall of cool grey
marble where every footstep rings. Niches in the walls hold busts of
bearded thinkers, their noses polished smooth by generations of hopeful
hands. Doors open north upon the forecourt, and the hall runs east and
west into the wings. To the south an arch frames the garden, a green
glow beyond it.

5702.name: The North Wing

east.description: To the east lies The Northern Side of the Academy.

west.description: To the west lies The Northwest Corner.

5702.description:
Portraits of former heads of the Academy hang along this stretch of the
North Wing in gilt frames, each more severe than the last. Between them
narrow shelves hold rolled maps tied with faded ribbon. The floor is
worn into two shallow troughs by the passage of countless feet. The
vestibule lies east, and the corner opens west.

5703.name: The Northwest Corner

east.description: To the east lies The North Wing.

south.description: To the south lies The West Wing.

5703.description:
The Northwest Corner is a round chamber with a domed ceiling pierced by
a lantern of coloured glass, which throws wandering rainbows on the
floor. A circular bench runs round the walls, and in the middle stands a
small table with a chessboard, its pieces locked in mid-argument. A
draught moves the dust. Corridors lead east along the North Wing and
south down the West Wing.

5704.name: The West Wing

north.description: To the north lies The Northwest Corner.

south.description: To the south lies The West Wing.

west.description: To the west lies Lecture room of Heraclitus.

5704.description:
The corridor widens into a bay at the foot of a little flight of steps.
A heavy door to the west stands open on the lecture room of Heraclitus,
and the faint sound of running water drifts from it. Pegs along the wall
hold dusty academic gowns of grey and brown. The West Wing runs south
from here, and the corner lies north.

5705.name: The West Wing

north.description: To the north lies The West Wing.

east.description: To the east lies In the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The West Wing.

5705.description:
The West Wing here is lined with doors of dark oak, each with a brass
plate engraved with the name of a master long dead. Long windows of
rippled glass throw wavering light across the floor. At the foot of the
wall a runner of faded red wool absorbs every step. The passage runs
north and south along the wing, and an arch on the east side opens onto
the garden.

5706.name: The West Wing

north.description: To the north lies The West Wing.

south.description: To the south lies The Southwest Corner.

west.description: To the west lies Lecture room on Stoicism.

5706.description:
A smell of woodsmoke and cabbage broth drifts along this stretch of the
West Wing from the kitchens beyond the walls. The plaster is yellow with
age, and a row of pegs holds nothing but a single forgotten scarf. A
stained board announces the hours of the lectures in a faded hand. To
the west a door stands ajar on the lecture room on Stoicism, and the
wing runs north and south.

5707.name: The Southwest Corner

north.description: To the north lies The West Wing.

east.description: To the east lies The South Wing.

5707.description:
The Southwest Corner is a dim, narrow place where two wings meet and
neither has much to say. A small window of greenish glass looks out on a
walled yard of firewood. A chipped bust of Zeno sits on a shelf, his
nose long since broken off. Passages lead north along the West Wing and
east along the South Wing.

5708.name: The South Wing

east.description: To the east lies Middle of the South Wing.

south.description: To the south lies The Dining Hall.

west.description: To the west lies The Southwest Corner.

5708.description:
The South Wing is wider here, with a vaulted ceiling hung with lamps of
tarnished brass and a smell of roast meat in the air. A pair of double
doors to the south stands open on the dining hall, from which comes the
clink of pewter. Rush matting lines the floor. The corridor leads west
to the corner and east along the wing.

5709.name: Middle of the South Wing

north.description: To the north lies In the Garden.

east.description: To the east lies The South Wing.

west.description: To the west lies The South Wing.

5709.description:
Midway along the South Wing an open archway looks north upon the garden,
where a white pavilion shows pale among the trees. A long runner of
threadbare carpet leads on, and a row of benches faces the wall as if
their sitters were waiting for a summons that never came. A clock of
water and brass drips patiently in a niche, marking hours no one keeps.
East and west the passage goes on along the wing.

5710.name: The South Wing

east.description: To the east lies The Southeast Corner.

south.description: To the south lies The Slave Quarters.

west.description: To the west lies Middle of the South Wing.

5710.description:
The South Wing is plainer than the others, its floor of worn flagstones
and its walls limewashed, with iron hooks at intervals for lanterns and
coats. A low door in the south wall has a rope handle in place of a
latch, and from behind it comes the smell of boiled barley and wet wool.
The corridor stretches west toward the middle of the wing and east to
the corner. The door south leads to the Slave Quarters.

5711.name: The Southeast Corner

north.description: To the north lies The East Wing.

west.description: To the west lies The South Wing.

5711.description:
In the Southeast Corner a window seat looks down through narrow panes on
a kitchen yard heaped with cabbage stalks and broken amphorae. The
plaster is patched here and the paint is older than that of the lecture
halls, a sign that the Academy's wealth thins toward the servants' end.
A brazier warms the angle against the draught. The passage leads north
along the East Wing and west into the South Wing.

5712.name: The East Wing

north.description: To the north lies The East Wing.

east.description: To the east lies Lecture room on Sophism.

south.description: To the south lies The Southeast Corner.

5712.description:
Here the East Wing grows narrower and the lamps burn brighter, as if the
Sophists wished their listeners to see every smile. Dried rose petals
lie swept into drifts along the skirting. A curtained archway to the
east opens into the lecture room on Sophism, where silver tongues are
trained. The passage runs north toward the garden arches and south to
the corner.

5713.name: The East Wing

north.description: To the north lies The East Wing.

south.description: To the south lies The East Wing.

west.description: To the west lies In the Garden.

5713.description:
Round arches open on the west side of the East Wing, giving long views
into the garden, where green leaves nod in a draught from nowhere. The
inner wall is hung with framed maps of lands the Academy's masters have
never visited, drawn from other men's reports. A brass drinking fountain
gurgles in a niche, its basin stained green. The corridor runs north and
south, and a gap in the arches leads west into the garden.

5714.name: The East Wing

north.description: To the north lies The Northeast Corner.

east.description: To the east lies Lecture Room on Logic.

south.description: To the south lies The East Wing.

5714.description:
The East Wing is panelled in dark oak to the height of a man, with brass
lamps burning in brackets at every third pace. A smell of beeswax and
old vellum hangs in the air. A heavy door stands open to the east upon
the Lecture Room on Logic, and the scrape of chalk on slate comes
faintly through it. The corridor runs on south and turns back north
toward the corner.

5715.name: The Northeast Corner

south.description: To the south lies The East Wing.

west.description: To the west lies The North Wing.

5715.description:
Two corridors meet at the Northeast Corner in a square little hall under
a ribbed ceiling painted midnight blue and scattered with gilt stars. A
bronze astrolabe the size of a cartwheel is bolted to the wall, its
rings still turning at a touch. A cushioned bench waits in the angle for
those who must think before they go on. The way south leads down the
East Wing, and the North Wing runs back west.

5716.name: The North Wing

east.description: To the east lies The Northeast Corner.

west.description: To the west lies The Northern Side of the Academy.

5716.description:
A broad corridor runs the length of the North Wing, its floor laid in
black and white squares like a board for some patient game. Tall windows
of thick greenish glass admit a watery light, and between them hang
tapestries of the Seven Sages, their threads gone dull. A rack of scroll
cases leans against the wall, each labelled in a cramped scholarly hand.
The passage ends east at a corner, and west it opens toward the
vestibule.

5717.name: Lecture room of Heraclitus

east.description: To the east lies The West Wing.

5717.description:
A shallow stone channel runs round the floor of this lecture room, fed
by a trickle from a spout in the wall, so that the sound of flowing
water is never absent. At the lectern a brazier of iron burns with a low
red flame fed by pitch. On the wall behind it, painted in tall black
letters, stands a saying about rivers and fire. Only one door leads out,
east to the West Wing.

extra_descs.saying painted letters river fire:
The saying is that no man steps twice into the same river, for it is not
the same river and he is not the same man.

5718.name: Lecture room on Stoicism

east.description: To the east lies The West Wing.

5718.description:
A bare room of whitewashed walls and a plain stone floor, without a
single ornament, for the Stoics held that comfort was a distraction.
Rows of backless benches face a low platform, and over its edge hangs a
coarse woollen curtain. Painted on the wall is a porch of columns, as
though to remind pupils of the school's origin. The only way out is
east, to the West Wing.

5719.name: The Dining Hall

north.description: To the north lies The South Wing.

5719.description:
A long hall of scrubbed oak tables and plain benches stretches under a
ceiling of dark beams, where lamps hang on chains. A great hearth fills
the end wall, its fire banked to embers beneath a spit and a row of iron
pots. Carved on the mantel are the names of every master since the
founding. Trestles stand stacked against the wall, and the only door is
north to the South Wing.

5720.name: The Slave Quarters

north.description: To the north lies The South Wing.

5720.description:
Rows of narrow plank bunks with straw pallets fill the long low room,
each with a peg above it holding one spare tunic. There is no window,
only a grating high in the wall that lets in a smear of grey light and
the smell of the kitchen. Names are scratched into the beams, some many
times over, some only once. A single door leads back north to the South
Wing.

5721.name: Lecture room on Sophism

west.description: To the west lies The East Wing.

5721.description:
A theatre in miniature: a curved dais of polished cedar faces a
semicircle of cushioned couches, with a gilded chair at its centre for
whoever is to be persuaded. Painted on the dome overhead are Gorgias,
Protagoras and their pupils, gesturing with enviable ease. Lamps on tall
tripods give a flattering honeyed light. A pitcher of wine stands stale
on the speaker's table, and the only way out is west to the East Wing.

5722.name: Lecture Room on Logic

west.description: To the west lies The East Wing.

down.description: To the down lies The Paradox Closet.

5722.description:
Rising tiers of oak benches face a lectern and a great slate wall
covered in chalked syllogisms, half rubbed out and rewritten in another
hand. Each bench has an inkwell sunk in its arm, and a few quills lie
where they were dropped. Behind the lectern a trapdoor of iron-studded
planks stands ajar upon a steep stair that leads down to the Paradox
Closet. The only other way out is west, to the East Wing.

5723.name: In the Garden

north.description: To the north lies The Northern Side of the Academy.

east.description: To the east lies In the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies In the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies In the Garden.

5723.description:
The garden begins here at the foot of an arch from the vestibule, where
an olive tree grows from a great clay tub and its silver leaves tremble
in the warm air. Box hedges are clipped into squares and spirals, and
gravel walks lead off between them. A low stone plaque set in the path
reads Nothing In Excess. The way north returns to the Northern Side of
the Academy, and paths wind east, south and west.

extra_descs.plaque path stone:
The plaque is old, and the lettering has been worn nearly smooth by
feet.

5724.name: In the Garden

north.description: To the north lies In the Garden.

east.description: To the east lies The East Wing.

south.description: To the south lies In the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies In the Garden.

5724.description:
A bronze sundial on a fluted pedestal stands at the meeting of four
paths, though no sun reaches it beneath the glass, and the gnomon casts
only a smudge of shadow. Arches in the wall to the east open into the
East Wing. Paths lead north to the vines, south to a corner of pear
trees, and west to the fountain. Lavender borders the gravel and scents
the damp air.

5725.name: In the Garden

north.description: To the north lies The Marble Pavillion.

east.description: To the east lies In the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies Middle of the South Wing.

west.description: To the west lies In the Garden.

5725.description:
Gravel paths cross here beneath a trellis of climbing roses that has
outgrown its frame and tumbled into the beds. A marble pavilion stands
north, its columns wreathed in ivy, and the path to it is worn pale by
feet. An arch in the wall to the south leads back into the South Wing.
Overhead the leaded glass of the roof is streaked and green, and the air
beneath it is damp and warm and smells of loam.

5726.name: In the Garden

north.description: To the north lies In the Garden.

east.description: To the east lies In the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies In the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The West Wing.

5726.description:
Raised herb beds of thyme, sage and bitter wormwood fill this part of
the garden, each labelled on a slate tablet in neat chalk. A rain barrel
of cracked oak stands under a drainpipe and hums with a faint insect
drone. The scent of crushed leaves hangs in the damp air. A broad arch
in the wall to the west leads into the West Wing, and paths run north,
east and south.

5727.name: In the Garden

north.description: To the north lies In the Garden.

east.description: To the east lies In the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies In the Garden.

5727.description:
A round fountain stands at the heart of the garden, its basin of grey
marble carved with leaping fish, though the spout has run dry and only
the mist of condensed air drips from the rim. Four paths meet at the
basin, each edged with trimmed hedges. Benches sit round it at even
intervals, as if for a conversation long ended. Paths lead north, east
and west from here.

5728.name: In the Garden

east.description: To the east lies In the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies In the Garden.

5728.description:
A single great pear tree, the oldest in the garden, spreads over a ring
of seats made from sawn logs, where disputations were once held. Its
fruit lies rotting in the grass in a sweet brown drift. The lattice of
the glass roof shows green with moss, and the light that gets through it
is dim and speckled. The path leads east and south.

5729.name: In the Garden

south.description: To the south lies In the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies In the Garden.

5729.description:
A grape arbour covers this corner of the garden, its vines trained over
a frame of white-painted iron until the leaves meet overhead in a green
tunnel. Bunches of small black fruit hang just out of reach. A stone
seat inside holds a sunken cushion and a forgotten volume of verse.
Paths run south toward the sundial and west along the far beds.

5730.name: In the Garden

north.description: To the north lies In the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies In the Garden.

5730.description:
A low wall along one side of this corner of the garden carries pear
trees trained flat against the stone, their fruit hard and green. A
stone bench sits in the angle with a cushion of moss on one arm. Gravel
crunches underfoot, and a path leads north toward a sundial and west
toward the roses. Rain has never fallen here, yet the leaves always
glisten.

5731.name: In the Garden

north.description: To the north lies In the Garden.

east.description: To the east lies In the Garden.

5731.description:
A small lily pond lies here, its stone rim worn into hollows by sitting
and its water dark as tea, with a few pale blossoms floating at the
edges. Moss has crept over the flagstones, and the air is thick with the
scent of damp earth. A path leads north toward the herb beds and east
toward the roses and a white pavilion.

5732.name: The Paradox Closet

south.description: To the south lies The Liar's Den.

up.description: To the up lies Lecture Room on Logic.

5732.description:
This cramped closet holds nothing but shelves of locked boxes, each
labelled This Box Is Empty and each heavy when lifted. A card pinned
over the door says Do Not Read This Card. The air is close and smells of
lamp oil and dust. A stair climbs up to the Lecture Room on Logic, and a
door in the far wall leads south to a gloomier chamber.

extra_descs.card pinned:
The card is written in a beautiful hand, and it is quite impossible to
read it without breaking its rule.

5733.name: The Liar's Den

north.description: To the north lies The Paradox Closet.

south.description: To the south lies The Arrow's Nest.

5733.description:
A low windowless room lit by a single swinging lamp, whose shadow never
seems to fall where it should. The same sentence is painted across the
walls in a dozen hands, All that is written here is false, and under
each someone has scrawled a furious rebuttal. Three-legged stools stand
round a table scarred with knife-points. A door north returns to the
Paradox Closet, and another south leads on.

5734.name: The Arrow's Nest

north.description: To the north lies The Liar's Den.

south.description: To the south lies The Eternal Race.

5734.description:
The ceiling of this long narrow chamber is hung with hundreds of painted
wooden arrows, each dangling on a thread and none ever seen to land. At
the end of the room a target of straw and canvas waits, always a little
farther off than it was. Dust lies thick on the boards where no one has
ever got across. The Liar's Den lies back north, and the room opens
south onto a running track.

5735.name: The Eternal Race

east.description: To the east lies The Paradox Closet.

south.description: To the south lies Further on the Race Track.

5735.description:
A running track of packed sand, ringed by a low wall, has been laid out
beneath an oval vault of whitewashed brick. Two sets of footprints are
pressed into it, one far ahead of the other, and neither pair seems to
have made any progress. A stone tortoise squats at the starting line,
polished smooth by passing palms. A door east returns to the Paradox
Closet, and the track bends south.

5736.name: Further on the Race Track

north.description: To the north lies The Eternal Race.

south.description: To the south lies Further on the Race Track.

5736.description:
The track goes on and on between low whitewashed walls hung with faded
pennants. Every few strides a marble post is numbered with a fraction,
one half, three quarters, seven eighths, each nearer the next than the
last. The sand is scuffed into long grooves by feet that never quite
arrive. Behind you the track runs back north to the starting line, and
ahead it looks exactly as it did before.

5750.name: The Maze under the Garden

north.description: To the north lies The Maze under the Garden.

east.description: To the east lies The Maze under the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The Maze under the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Maze under the Garden.

up.description: To the up lies The Marble Pavillion.

5750.description:
The stair ends in a low brick chamber where several passages begin at
once and none looks different from another. Water beads the walls, and
the air is thick, warm and faintly sweet, like meat left too long in a
larder. A chalked arrow on the floor has been scuffed out and redrawn so
many times that it points at nothing. The steps behind you are lost
already in the gloom.

5751.name: The Maze under the Garden

north.description: To the north lies The Maze under the Garden.

east.description: To the east lies The Maze under the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The Maze under the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Maze under the Garden.

up.description: To the up lies The Maze under the Garden.

down.description: To the down lies The Maze under the Garden.

5751.description:
The walls here are daubed with white paint in looping symbols that might
be a mathematician's despair or a lost student's last attempt at a map.
A rope hangs from a hatch in the ceiling, frayed at the end where it was
cut. A drain in the floor gurgles and breathes out warm air. Every
turning looks like the one before it.

5752.name: The Maze under the Garden

north.description: To the north lies The Maze under the Garden.

east.description: To the east lies The Maze under the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The Maze under the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Maze under the Garden.

up.description: To the up lies The Maze under the Garden.

down.description: To the down lies The Maze under the Garden.

5752.description:
Rusted rings are set in the walls of this junction, as though something
was once tethered here, and the brick beneath them is scored with long
grooves. A narrow ladder of iron staples climbs into a black slot
overhead, and another drops into a hole in the floor. Passages leave in
every direction, and all of them smell the same: wet clay, lamp soot and
something sweetly rotten.

5753.name: The Maze under the Garden

east.description: To the east lies The Maze under the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The Maze under the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Maze under the Garden.

up.description: To the up lies The Maze under the Garden.

down.description: To the down lies The Maze under the Garden.

5753.description:
A round chamber with a domed ceiling of small bricks, where a dry
whisper returns your own footsteps a moment late and slightly altered.
Broken crockery lies in a ring on the floor, bowls and cups pitched
against the wall in some old tantrum. A hole in the floor shows a dim
glow far below, and a ladder of staples climbs into the dome above.

5754.name: The Maze under the Garden

east.description: To the east lies The Maze under the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The Maze under the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Maze under the Garden.

up.description: To the up lies The Maze under the Garden.

down.description: To the down lies The Maze under the Garden.

5754.description:
The passage narrows to a throat barely wide enough for a man's
shoulders, the bricks bulging inward as if something enormous pressed on
them from the far side. A stair of worn wedge-shaped steps climbs one
way and another descends the other. Scratches at the height of a hand
cover the stone, thousands of them, in groups of five. The smell is
stronger here.

5755.name: The Maze under the Garden

north.description: To the north lies The Maze under the Garden.

east.description: To the east lies The Maze under the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The Maze under the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Maze under the Garden.

up.description: To the up lies A Tiny Niche.

down.description: To the down lies The Maze under the Garden.

5755.description:
Lamp brackets in the walls hold stubs of tallow candles burned down to
puddles, the remains of an expedition that lit its way and still lost
it. A bent iron grate lies in a corner with a bundle of mouldering rags
beside it. A cramped stair spirals up toward a small niche, and another
spiral drops away below. The air feels thick, as if it had been breathed
many times.

5756.name: The Maze under the Garden

north.description: To the north lies The Maze under the Garden.

east.description: To the east lies The Maze under the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The Maze under the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Maze under the Garden.

down.description: To the down lies The Maze under the Garden.

5756.description:
Raised on a plinth in the middle of this chamber is a stone bust of a
man with his eyes gouged out and his mouth stopped with clay. A gutter
circles the plinth and carries a thin dark trickle into a hole to one
side. Steps lead down into a lower passage. The walls sweat, and green-
black stains creep from the floor to the ceiling.

extra_descs.bust plinth stone:
The bust is of Phaeton himself, to judge by the heavy brow and the proud
chin. Someone has taken a chisel to the eyes.

5757.name: The Maze under the Garden

north.description: To the north lies The Maze under the Garden.

east.description: To the east lies Behind the Secret Panel.

south.description: To the south lies The Maze under the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Maze under the Garden.

up.description: To the up lies The Maze under the Garden.

down.description: To the down lies The Maze under the Garden.

5757.description:
The brickwork gives way here to a stretch of smooth black stone, as
though a different hand built this corner of the maze. In the wall to
the east a panel the width of a door, edged with a hairline seam, stands
slightly proud of the stone. A handprint in the dust beside it shows
where someone has often pushed it open. Passages continue in other
directions, and stairs lead both up and down.

5758.name: The Maze under the Garden

north.description: To the north lies The Maze under the Garden.

east.description: To the east lies The Maze under the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The Maze under the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Maze under the Garden.

up.description: To the up lies The Maze under the Garden.

5758.description:
Bones of small animals, rats and cats and one that might have been a
dog, lie in drifts along the foot of the walls, picked clean and set in
neat rows. A net of dark wire sags from the ceiling, torn through in the
middle. The roof is low enough to brush your hair, and a narrow stair
rises into the dark overhead. Something has been collecting here, and
carefully.

5759.name: The Maze under the Garden

north.description: To the north lies On the Landing before the Study.

east.description: To the east lies The Maze under the Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The Maze under the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Maze under the Garden.

up.description: To the up lies The Maze under the Garden.

down.description: To the down lies The Maze under the Garden.

5759.description:
The maze loosens its grip a little here: the floor is swept, and a brass
lamp with a clean wick burns in a bracket at the head of a short flight
of steps. Long streaks on the brick show where something heavy has been
dragged in and out. A lit landing to the north promises order, and the
stench thins as you near it. Passages lead off on every other hand.

5760.name: On the Landing before the Study

north.description: To the north lies The Maze under the Garden.

east.description: To the east lies Phaeton's Secret Study.

south.description: To the south lies The Maze under the Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Maze under the Garden.

5760.description:
A small stone landing, swept and lamp-lit, lies before a door of black
walnut bound with silver. A mat of woven reed is laid at the threshold,
and above the lintel hangs a brass plate engraved with a name and a
short warning to visitors. Dust has been brushed from the handle by a
hand that comes often. The door stands east, and the maze closes in
again to the north, west and south.

5761.name: Phaeton's Secret Study

west.description: To the west lies On the Landing before the Study.

5761.description:
Books climb to the ceiling in crooked towers, and every flat surface
bears a clutter of astrolabes, retorts, bell jars and loose pages
crawling with equations. A great desk of dark wood sits under a lamp of
green glass, an open journal upon it in a hurried hand. Glass tanks
along one wall hold pale pickled shapes that were never quite natural.
The only way out is west, back to the landing.

extra_descs.journal open desk:
The last entries are cramped and damp-stained, recording an experiment
that was to join the wisdom of many minds in a single body. The final
line says only that it has outgrown its cage.

5762.name: A Tiny Niche

west.description: To the west lies The Refuge of Erasmos.

down.description: To the down lies The Maze under the Garden.

5762.description:
A hole barely large enough to crouch in has been scraped from the brick
and lined with sacking. A candle stub sits in a saucer beside a clay
cup, and chalk marks on the wall count days in fives, then stop. A low
door of planks leads west, and a spiral stair drops back down into the
maze. The air here is a little cleaner, and someone has tried to keep it
so.

5763.name: The Refuge of Erasmos

east.description: To the east lies A Tiny Niche.

5763.description:
A tidy tiny chamber, arranged by someone who refused to go mad. A narrow
cot is made up with a folded blanket, a shelf holds a few salvaged
books, and a ledger on an upturned crate logs the days in a steady hand.
Chalked proofs cover one wall beside a map of the maze with many
corrections. The only way out is east, to the niche.

5764.name: Behind the Secret Panel

west.description: To the west lies The Maze under the Garden.

5764.description:
This cramped closet behind the panel is narrow as a wardrobe, its walls
lined with shelves of stoppered jars whose labels have faded to brown
ghosts. A sheet of sketches pinned to the plaster shows a creature drawn
again and again, each version a little less like anything alive. The
panel swings shut behind you with a soft click and a sigh of mortar
dust. The air is stale and tastes of vinegar.

5765.name: The Marble Pavillion

south.description: To the south lies In the Garden.

down.description: To the down lies The Maze under the Garden.

5765.description:
Eight slender columns hold up a domed roof of white marble, and the
floor is a mosaic of interlocking squares in cream and rose. At the
centre a round stone cover the width of a cartwheel has been set into
the floor, ringed with brass and furrowed by chains. Beneath it a stair
plunges down into dankness, and a warm sour breath rises from it. The
garden lies south, bright and green, but the pavilion itself feels
watched.

649900.name: scholar academic student man
649900.long_desc: A pale scholar in a grey gown stands muttering over a scroll.
649900.description:
He is thin and ink-fingered, with the unhealthy pallor of one who reads
by lamplight. A leather satchel of scrolls hangs at his hip, and he
looks up at strangers with absent, patient annoyance.

649901.name: slave servant man
649901.long_desc: A weary slave in a rough tunic goes about his chores with lowered eyes.
649901.description:
A lean, stooped man with a brand on his forearm and rope-calloused
hands. He keeps his gaze on the floor and moves as if every footstep
were measured against a lash.

649902.name: rat giant maze
649902.long_desc: A giant maze rat the size of a hound scuttles along the wall with its yellow teeth bared.
649902.description:
Its fur is sleek, almost glossy, and its eyes are the wrong colour, a
flat and thoughtful green. It moves along the passages as if it knew
them very well.

649903.name: bronze golem automaton guardian
649903.long_desc: A towering bronze golem stands guard, its green-veined joints creaking with each slow breath of steam.
649903.description:
The golem is twice the height of a man, cast in the likeness of a
bearded sage with a hammer for a hand. Verdigris crusts its seams, and a
thin steam escapes from a vent in its back with a faint hissing wheeze.

649904.name: arch sophist rhetorician master man
649904.long_desc: An arch sophist in silk robes stands upon the dais, smiling the smile of a man who has never lost an argument.
649904.description:
He is handsome and sleek, with oiled curls and rings on every finger,
and a voice like warm honey. His eyes, though, are quite cold, and they
measure you for the price of your purse.

649905.name: aporia failed experiment chimera beast
649905.long_desc: Aporia the failed experiment lurches through the passage, a patchwork thing of many mismatched limbs.
649905.description:
A sprawling heap of flesh and hide stitched together from a dozen
creatures, scholar, hound and ox, it drags a trailing arm and murmurs
half-remembered syllogisms in a dozen voices. Its eyes are set in the
wrong places and all of them are weeping.

649906.name: phaeton wizard philosopher master
649906.long_desc: Phaeton, master of the Academy, bends over his desk with ink on his cuffs and madness in his eyes.
649906.description:
A tall gaunt man in a threadbare black gown, with a hawk's nose and
white hair standing in tufts. He mutters in Greek and in numbers, and a
staff of pale ash glows faintly in his fist. The brilliance in his eyes
has long since curdled into something else.

749900.name: bronze stylus pointed
749900.room_desc: A pointed bronze stylus lies here.
749900.description: A scribe's stylus of bronze, long and sharp, with a flattened end for scraping out mistakes. It will serve as a dagger in a pinch.

749901.name: honeyed barley cake
749901.room_desc: A honeyed barley cake sits here, wrapped in a cloth.
749901.description: A dense little cake of barley meal sweetened with dark honey, baked in the Academy's kitchens.

749902.name: bronze plate golem breastplate
749902.room_desc: A greenish bronze breastplate lies here.
749902.description: A piece torn from a golem's chest, heavy, green with verdigris and engraved with tiny rows of numbers. Hammered into a fit, it makes a stout cuirass.

749903.name: silver ring sophist
749903.room_desc: A silver ring set with a polished stone lies here.
749903.description: A silver band whose inner side is inscribed with a very small, very clever argument. The wearer feels a little sharper in the head.

749904.name: knotted hide cloak
749904.room_desc: A cloak of stitched and knotted hide lies here.
749904.description: A cloak stitched from many hides of different animals, tough and ill-smelling, with a knot at the clasp that no hand can untie.

749905.name: ash staff phaeton pale
749905.room_desc: A pale ash staff, faintly warm to the eye, lies here.
749905.description: A staff of pale ash, carved with spiralling equations from foot to crown. It hums gently when swung, and the wood is faintly warm.
